english: Let $N_1$ denote the number of $3\times3$ matrices, each of whose entries is $0$ or $1$, having exactly four entries equal to $1$, and let $N_2$ denote the number of those matrices that are symmetric. Then the value of $\dfrac{N_1}{N_2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $N_1$ उन $3\times3$ आव्यूहों की संख्या है, जिनकी प्रत्येक प्रविष्टि $0$ या $1$ है तथा जिनकी ठीक चार प्रविष्टियाँ $1$ के बराबर हैं, और $N_2$ इनमें से सममित आव्यूहों की संख्या है। तब $\dfrac{N_1}{N_2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $N_1$: select the $4$ positions of the $1$'s from $9$: $\binom94=126$
Symmetric: a $1$ at $(i,j)$, $i\neq j$, forces a $1$ at $(j,i)$; with $d$ ones on the diagonal and $p$ symmetric off-diagonal pairs, $d+2p=4$, $d\le3$
solution_full: A $0$-$1$ matrix with exactly four $1$'s is fixed by the set of positions of its $1$'s, a selection of $4$ of the $9$ positions. So $N_1=\binom94=\dfrac{9\cdot8\cdot7\cdot6}{24}=126$.
For a symmetric matrix, the positions split into the $3$ diagonal places and $3$ off-diagonal pairs $\{(i,j),(j,i)\}$, $i<j$; the two entries of a pair are equal.
If $d$ diagonal entries and $p$ pairs are $1$, the number of $1$'s is $d+2p=4$ with $0\le d\le3$, $0\le p\le3$. So $(d,p)=(2,1)$ or $(0,2)$ ($d=4$ is impossible).
Case $(2,1)$: select $2$ of the $3$ diagonal places and $1$ of the $3$ pairs: $\binom32\binom31=9$.
originality_note: New: a ratio of an unrestricted count to a symmetric count of 0-1 matrices with a fixed number of 1s; the symmetric count is a selection of diagonal places and off-diagonal pairs under d + 2p = 4 (way 5). Closest known: JEE Advanced 2009 paragraph on symmetric 0-1 matrices with five 1s (count 12). Different because: four 1s change the cases, and the question compares with the unrestricted selection C(9,4).
blueprint_concepts: Counting matrices satisfying given conditions (symmetric, trace, entries)

concept_use.Counting matrices satisfying given condi: Symmetric 0-1 matrices with four 1s are counted through d + 2p = 4 (diagonal ones and symmetric pairs), giving N2 = 12.
concept_use.Selection of r objects from n distinct o: N1 = C(9,4) = 126 selects the positions of the four 1s, and the cases of N2 select diagonal places and pairs with C(3,2) and C(3,1).

stem_review: Read as a student: every matrix and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked: brute force over all 2^9 matrices gives N1 = 126 and N2 = 12, so N1/N2 = 10.5 (a positive decimal as planned). Changed: No change.
key_step: Splitting the symmetric count by d + 2p = 4 into diagonal places and off-diagonal pairs, and comparing with C(9,4).
justification: Two linked counts (a plain selection and a structured symmetric count with two cases) in numerical form. Above the routine matrix count of 2024-P1-Q14 (L2); comparable to the bounded counting of 2026-P1-Q11 (L3). It could be read as a strong L2, hence Medium.
